subject.title: fix(worktrees): reclaim git worktree locks left by dead processes

question: Should dead-lock acquisition reclaim ship before the shared exclusive guard described in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/114129 is implemented across every reclaim path?
rationale: The PR fixes a production availability regression, but choosing between immediate partial recovery and preserving strict mutual exclusion under concurrent reclaim is a safety tradeoff that code review cannot safely resolve without maintainer intent.

options.title: Implement the shared guard first
options.body: Extend this work so every dead-lock reclaim path holds one worktree-scoped guard across observation and unlock, then merge the availability fix.

options.title: Accept the interim race explicitly
options.body: Merge the focused availability repair now and accept the rare concurrent-reclaim risk until the linked guard work lands.

options.title: Pause the acquire-side reclaim
options.body: Keep the current failure behavior until a comprehensive reclaim design is ready.

recommendation.title: Implement the shared guard first
recommendation.body: Extend this work so every dead-lock reclaim path holds one worktree-scoped guard across observation and unlock, then merge the availability fix.

likelyOwner.reason: The adjacent technical analysis identifies the affected call sites and the proposed shared-guard direction.
